To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) nuclear DGK-ζ is expressed in proliferative and differentiated C2C12 muscle cells, (ii) DGK-ζ overexpression induces a G1 arrest of proliferating C2C12, whereas its down-regulation by siRNA induces an S/G2/M arrest in differentiating cells, (iii) the G1 arrest of DGK-ζ-overexpressing C2C12 is due to a decreased phosphorylation of retinoblastoma protein, and
nuclear diacylglycerole kinase‐ζ (DGK‐ζ) is a negative regulator that controls the cell cycle progression in mouse myoblast cells.

nuclear diacylglycerols kinases (DGs), i.e. the enzymes that, converting diacylgycerol (DG) in phosphatidic acids, terminate DG-dependent events, are involved in the regulation of the cell cycle progression.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a nuclear enzyme, the diacylglycerole kinase‐ζ, that is able to block the cell cycle in G1 phase, by interfering with the retino‐blast protein phosphorylation, a major regulator of the cell cycle progression.
the identification of the mechanisms that regulate cell proliferation and differentiation.
the study of the nuclear localization and the biological role of the nuclear diacylglycerold kinases.

nuclear diacylglycerokinase ζ is a key negative regulator of the cell cycle progression in mouse myoblast cells.
DGK‐ζ is a key negative regulator of cell differentiation and cell cycle progression in myoblastic cells.
the nuclear DGK‐zeta is a negative regulator for cell cycle progression and cell differentiation in the C2C12 muscle cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

nuclear DGKζ, by converting di-acylglycerol into phosphatidate, terminates the signaling of di-acylgly- cerol, which is a second messenger of the phosphatidylcholine-specific phospho-lipase C (PLC) and is involved in the control of the cell cycle progression and myogenic differentiation of C2-C12 cells.
nuclear DGK-ζ is a key regulator of cell cycle and myoblast differentiation.
nuclear DGKζ is a key negative regulator of myoblastic cell cycle progression, and its down‐regula‐tion prevents cell cycle block characteriz‐ing myogenic differentiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nuclear DGK-ζ plays a role in regulating the cell cycle of muscle cells, in particular, in the G1/S phase.
nuclear diacylglycerold kinases (DGKS) are involved in cell cycle control and differentiation.
the nuclear diacylglycerold kinase (DGK)‐ζ, which is a negative regulator, is involved in cell cycle regulation.
